findings.summary: The studio half of FR-THM-005/007/009 is in no row and no gate leg. The plan goal says 'Themes become a studio feature — accessible palettes generated from seed colours or an image, ... a live theme editor, DTCG import/export and CSS variables'. FR-THM-007 is 'Theme editor UI with live preview; save/import/export theme files'. ADR-0055 §Image → palette says 'the editor decodes with createImageBitmap to <= 256 px longest side and passes ImageData's fields'. palette-image.ts says 'the editor passes ImageData's fields'. In fact nothing outside packages/theme and the SDK re-exports calls paletteFromPixels, exportDtcg, importDtcg, themesFromFiles or themeToCss. The M20.11 panel has role inputs, three seed inputs, Generate, Shuffle and variant previews, and no image input or theme file / DTCG / CSS import or export. M20.6, M20.8 and M20.9 were written as library acceptance, and M20.11's acceptance names only the primary-colour live preview, so every row closed honestly while the plan item slipped between them. M20.24 owes docs pages for 'palette, DTCG' that would describe studio actions that do not exist.

findings.summary: The rule 'the theme a screen draws with' (screen.themeId, else the applied master's, else document.themeId, else the light theme) now has three separate copies: render/src/screen-theme.ts useScreenTheme (plus screen-view's master lookup), dsl/src/lint/contrast.ts screenContext, and editor/src/theme-editor/theme-edit.ts themeHolders/editedTheme. The first review round of M20.10 (F1 and F2: screen background and theme per screen) and of M20.11 (F1: the applied master's theme skipped) each found a copy that had already drifted from the renderer. The copies differ in small ways. Render requires typeof themeId === 'string' and dsl uses ??. Render rebuilds the theme from name/tokens/defaults/tableStyles, while dsl and editor call themeOf on the whole record. These differences are harmless today. A fourth copy is due with SVG export (M20.12), where the exporter must pick the same theme.

findings.summary: Confirmed (known item). For each FLX_LINT_CONTRAST finding, contrastFix calls elementContrastIssues(doc, id, LIGHT_THEME). That builds a new read-only store of the whole document (contrast.ts:134 viewOf) and re-derives the screen context, which the lint pass had already computed. ProblemsTab runs problemsOf on every store revision, and M20.11 makes every colour-input event a revision. So with the Problems tab open, a document with k low-contrast elements and n records costs O(k*n) store builds per pick. That works against the theme editor's within-one-frame goal. The lint finding already carries the fix colour in its hint, so the work is duplicated.

Confirmed (known item). After M20.37 r1, completed infrastructure-miss runs are counted in the 'newer' list of a red run. The RED line then says '(N newer runs pending)' when some of those runs have finished, and they count toward LAST_CI_MAX_PENDING. Both effects push toward stopping (an earlier 'stop landing'), never toward a false green.

dispositions.note: New row M20.38 (FR-THM-005, FR-THM-007, FR-THM-009; deps M20.11), studio theme files and image seeds. WHEN a user picks an image in the theme editor THE SYSTEM SHALL decode it outside packages/theme (createImageBitmap, <= 256 px, as ADR-0055 says), fill the seed inputs from paletteFromPixels and generate the palette in one undo step. WHEN a user exports the edited theme THE SYSTEM SHALL download <slug>.tokens.json (exportDtcg) and, as a separate action, a .css file (themeToCss). WHEN a user imports a Fluxion or foreign DTCG file THE SYSTEM SHALL add it as a theme record in one undo step and list importDtcg's warnings. This is shown by exact-title browser cases in packages/editor/src/theme-editor/theme-editor.browser.test.tsx that m20-complete's FR-THM-005, FR-THM-007 and FR-THM-009 legs name, plus an e2e step in e2e/theme.editor-live.spec.ts or a new spec under the same three-engine and axe leg. The editor's initial gzip stays within EDITOR_INITIAL_GZIP (the code lives in the lazy panel chunk). M20.24 depends on it.

New row M20.39 (FR-THM-004, FR-THM-006, NFR-A11Y-005, HARNESS; before M20.12). Add one pure helper in core (e.g. screenTheme(view, screenId) returning the holder record and the theme record id, in ADR-0152/ADR-0054 order) with a case for each step of the order and for an invalid or missing record. render's useScreenTheme, dsl's screenContext and the editor's editedTheme/themeHolders call it, and M20.12's SVG exporter uses it too. Existing tests stay green unchanged.

Same row M20.39. problemsOf builds no store per contrast finding. Either the CONTRAST finding carries its fix colour and field as data, or problemsOf builds one view per pass and hands it to the fix. A problems.test case shows one view built per problemsOf call (an injected or counted builder), or, if timing is the measure, the theme-edit browser case stays in one frame with the Problems tab open.

The reason: M20.6-M20.11 each had library-level acceptance, so the studio surfaces fell between the rows (F1). Two copies of the screen-theme rule needed review-round fixes, which pointed to the third and to the shared helper (F2). Since cp3 the run has been healthy: six feature rows (M20.6-M20.11) and M20.37 in eight commits, no Fixes-ci rows, CI green at e04b0ef, and 0 flaky in e2e-report. Lessons for later milestones: when a plan goal says 'studio feature', a row and a gate case must name the UI entry point, not only the library function, and a rule needed by render, lint, editor and export belongs in core before its second copy.
